title: Focused IBM OM cap-128 endpoint model for DRN HWA
hypothesis: A lower-from-RESET, half-step-tolerance, 128-pulse adaptive program-and-verify characterization can retain the endpoint, failure, corruption, saturation, and cost information required by the DRN HWA pilot while avoiding full target sweeps for the one-pulse calibration controller, the unused upper-start direction, and the deferred HfO2 stress control.
motivation: The earlier short-production matrix spends most of its runtime on two controllers, two start directions, and both OM and HfO2 populations. The network pilot consumes only the OM adaptive lower-from-RESET condition. This focused study therefore records one-pulse trajectories only for the 20% calibration identities, records adaptive trajectories for all identities, and uses each fixed identity's sampled persistent lower/upper bounds for analysis-only reachability classification. It does not replace or reinterpret the broader immutable cap-128 comparison study.

arms.description: OM fixed-bound population with published corruption disabled; calibration-only one-pulse and full adaptive lower-from-RESET trajectories.
Matched OM population with the published corrupt/stuck probability enabled.

completion_criteria: Both arms complete exactly 201392 trajectories: 816 calibration-identity one-pulse trajectories and 4096 all-identity adaptive trajectories at each of 41 targets, for 402784 total trajectories.

Both runs record profile hwa_production_cap128, OM preset, 1024 identities, four repeats, lower_to_target only, tau/step=0.5, maximum_program_pulses=128, and the unchanged 0.2/0.6/0.2 identity partition.
The one-pulse controller observes only calibration identities and initializes the adaptive population estimator; its endpoint condition is not used as a fitted HWA model.

The adaptive condition has 2464 fit and 816 held-out validation trajectories per target before corruption filtering and passes the predeclared piecewise-uniform coverage and normalized target-binned Wasserstein adequacy gates.
Every non-corrupt adaptive trajectory is classified against its fixed sampled persistent lower/upper bounds without exposing either bound to the controller.
Both ledgers pass exact controller-specific trajectory-count, pulse/event, seed, identity, conditioning, and endpoint integrity checks.
The immutable HWA device bundle is built only if both adaptive endpoint conditions are adequate and embeds the endpoint and step-estimator source hashes.
analysis_plan: Fit the accepted non-corrupt residual density, failure terminals, corrupt/stuck terminals, saturation, and cost only from the adaptive lower-from-RESET condition; retain the one-pulse rows as controller-calibration evidence.
Use fit identities for model parameters and validation identities for coverage, target-binned Wasserstein distance, reachability-probability error, and all adequacy decisions.
Classify reachability with sampled fixed lower/upper persistent bounds. Keep exact target reachability, acceptance-window intersection, apparent acceptance, and persistent residual separate.

Report trajectory and verify-event reductions relative to the broader two-start, two-controller, four-preset cap-128 design, without treating omitted HfO2 or upper-start conditions as negative results.

Compare the adequate IBM OM apparent endpoint residual with Wan-2022 in the common normalized coordinate and preserve the distinct corruption, failure, pulse-cost, timing, and physical-calibration boundaries.
